title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option P2: British America, 1713–83: empire and revolution

exam_structure.overview: Tests unfolding period narrative across 3 Key Topics. Q1 Explain two consequences (8m), Q2 Write an analytical narrative (8m), Q3 Explain the importance of two events (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: British settlement in North America, 1713–41

topics.title: 1. Developments in colonial society
points: Impact of expansion & immigration on society: the pattern of settlement & tensions among social groups
Economic developments: trade with Britain & with the West Indies, tobacco, the impact of piracy (incl. the activities of ‘Black Sam’ Bellamy & Edward Teach (‘Blackbeard’)
Suppression of piracy in American waters: King George I’s Proclamation & the Piracy Act (1717), the work of Governor Spotswood

topics.title: 2. Slavery in North America
points: Transatlantic slave trade & ‘Atlantic trade triangle’
Impact of slavery on the development of tobacco & rice plantations
Impact of slavery on colonial society; the position of enslaved people within society & the treatment of fugitives within the colonies

topics.title: 3. Problems within the colonies
points: Slave revolts in the Carolinas: the Stono Rebellion (1739); Spain’s decision to protect runaways in Florida
The New York Conspiracy (1741)
Smuggling, attempts to collect customs revenue & to control the fur trade

topics.title: 1. The impact of cultural developments
points: Religious revivals (incl. the Great Awakening & revivalist preachers)
The Enlightenment: the emphasis on education; the growth of newspapers & public libraries
Significance: Benjamin Franklin as a writer, philanthropist & intellectual

topics.title: 2. War in the colonies
points: Relations with the French & with Indigenous peoples during & after King George’s War (1744–48)
The French & Indian War (1754–63) in North America & Wolfe in Canada
Significance: Treaty of Paris (1763) & the Proclamation Act (1763)

topics.title: 3. The aftermath of the French and Indian war
points: Impact of the war on American colonists’ relations with Britain
Opposition to the Sugar Act (1764)
Relations with Indigenous peoples (incl. Pontiac’s Rebellion (1763–64); The Paxton Boys: their actions & impact

sections.title: Key topic 3: The loss of an empire, 1765–83

topics.title: 1. American colonist relations with Britain: growing opposition, 1765-75
points: Opposition to British policies: the Stamp Act, the Sons of Liberty & the Boston Massacre (1770)
British & American relations: the Boston Tea Party (1773) & the Intolerable Acts (1774)
Significance: First & Second Continental Congresses, 1774–75

topics.title: 2. The War of Independence 1775-83
points: Influence of Thomas Paine's 'Common Sense'; Declaration of Independence; Thomas Jefferson
Key American victories: Saratoga (1777) & Yorktown (1781); Washington’s role, British mistakes & French & Spanish involvement in the war
The Peace of Paris (1783) (incl. Franklin)

topics.title: 3. Consequences of the war in America
points: Significance: American independence for slavery
Consequences of the war for Indigenous peoples
Impact of the war on Loyalists (incl. their resettlement in Nova Scotia & Niagara)
